step_1_analysis.description: Analyzed core message of each slide to determine visual communication need

messages_identified.SL01: Convergence of multiple factors creating opportunity
messages_identified.SL05: Category alignment between EF and SCIS
messages_identified.SL09: Budget stagnation vs purchasing power decline
messages_identified.SL11: Reinforcing loop between EF and KAKENHI

step_2_visual_selection.description: Selected optimal visual format for each slide's message type

rationale.avoided_defaults: No pie charts used; bar charts used sparingly and only for direct comparison
rationale.relationship_focus: Used Venn diagrams and loop diagrams to show interdependencies
rationale.action_orientation: Final slides use timeline and summary formats to drive action

step_3_specifications.description: Created detailed specifications for each visual
specification_elements: Component definitions with IDs, labels, shapes, colors
Data series with specific values where available

step_4_takeaways.description: Wrote explicit takeaway statements for all 15 visuals
step_4_takeaways.takeaway_pattern: Each takeaway states the conclusion the audience should draw, not just what the visual shows

design_principles_applied: Gene Zelazny: Match visual type to message type (comparison, trend, relationship)
Edward Tufte: Maximize data-ink ratio, avoid chartjunk
Information hierarchy: Primary message in largest/most prominent element
Action orientation: Final slides designed to drive specific behavior
